solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Process of brooding?

parts.note: brooding here is a hen sitting on eggs to hatch them, not a person sulking

explanation.surface: A question about how moody thinking works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooding' wants to mean dark, gloomy thought; the question mark points to the hen keeping her eggs warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting on eggs to keep them warm until they hatch is the bird's way of hatching its young.

clue.text: Proclamation of Welsh politician and spiritual leader

parts.note: the politician's declaration of who they are, 'I'm', the start of 'I'm an Assembly Member'
AM, Assembly Member, a member of the Welsh Assembly

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician's announcement, set beside a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: An AM is a member of the Welsh Assembly; this is what one might announce when introducing themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The man who leads prayers in a mosque is the Muslim spiritual leader of the congregation.

clue.text: Opportunist in section of church switching direction

indicators.note: left becomes right: the letter L, for left, swaps for R, for right

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar

explanation.surface: Someone taking a chance in a part of the church while turning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching direction' changes the L (left) in CHANCEL into R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes risks to get ahead, grabbing whatever chance arises, is an opportunist.

clue.text: A race at a club getting fancy European award

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A race held at a club wins an elaborate prize from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ARACEATACLUB; E (European) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The baccalaureate is a qualification or degree conferred, so an academic award.

clue.text: Rule set in rowdy feeding place

indicators.note: the letter for rule is placed inside the word for rowdy

parts.note: tough, as in a tough neighbourhood or a rough, rowdy type

explanation.surface: A regulation imposed in a noisy place where animals eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in' puts R (rule) inside TOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A long open container from which livestock eat is a place where animals are fed.

clue.text: Men admitting first note on cross is sound

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another comes before it

parts.note: OR, other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
admitting that is 'though', shortened informally to tho
do (doh) is the first note of the sol-fa scale
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Soldiers conceding that an opening note on a cross sounds right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' gives THO (though, as in 'admitting that'); 'on' puts DO above X in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of conventional and correct in belief or opinion means orthodox.

clue.text: Club payments coming directly from the North?

parts.note: due, as in due south, means exactly or directly
someone travelling from the north is heading S, south

explanation.surface: Subscriptions to a club arriving straight from the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as DUE S: travelling directly away from the north is heading due south.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular fees paid by members of a club or society are their subscriptions.

clue.text: Posh ministerial aide getting dressed in Swedish city

parts.note: U means upper-class, so posh
PPS, a Parliamentary Private Secretary, assists a British minister
à la means prepared or dressed in the manner of, as in cooking

explanation.surface: A smart government aide putting on clothes in Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: A PPS is a junior MP who assists a government minister in Britain; ALA is 'à la', prepared in a given manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a university city north of Stockholm in Sweden.

clue.text: This wear's sported over front of torso?

definitions.text: This wear's sported over front of torso?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece over another comes before it
sported means displayed or shown off, so the letters are worn in a new arrangement
the front of the word torso is its first letter

explanation.surface: This garment is worn over the upper body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sported' rearranges THISWEARS; 'front of' torso gives T, placed below. The whole clue also describes the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cotton jersey is the kind of top pulled on over the chest and back.

clue.text: A sailor docked with company around island capital

indicators.note: docked means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: jack is slang for a sailor, as in jack tar

indicators.note: the abbreviation for company goes round the letter for island

explanation.surface: A sailor in port with his ship's company around an island's main city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the sailor's last letter; 'around' wraps company round island. A ship docking is the false scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajaccio is the chief city of Corsica, an island and French region, so a capital.

clue.text: Thrilling experiences touring area to East in walk

indicators.note: the word for thrilling experiences travels round the letter for area

parts.note: trips, as in drug-induced excitement or a buzz

explanation.surface: Exciting outings across a region to the east, done on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts TRIPS round A, then E (east) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge about wearily or aimlessly is a kind of walking.

clue.text: Boost run-down area this month

indicators.note: run-down means dilapidated, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A neglected neighbourhood gets a lift this month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run-down' looks like a description of the area; it rearranges AREATHISMONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: An injection of encouragement or energy is an idiomatic lift or stimulus.

clue.text: Shifted position in earth?

parts.note: the five letters of earth are a rearrangement of the letters of heart

explanation.surface: Something has moved from its place in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange HEART and you get EARTH, so 'earth' is what a reshuffled heart looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversing an opinion or attitude is moving to a different stance.

clue.text: Spiteful mood about to disappear after sign of victory

indicators.note: the grammatical mood comes after the sign of victory

parts.note: V, the victory sign made with two fingers

indicators.note: the letter for about is removed from the word for the mood

parts.note: the indicative is a grammatical mood of verbs

explanation.surface: A bad temper ready to vanish after a gesture of triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mood' is grammar, not temper. 'about to disappear' removes A from the mood; 'after' places it behind the victory sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking revenge and wishing harm on others is malicious, mean-spirited behaviour.

clue.text: Encroachment delivering small medicinal box promotion

parts.note: an inro is a small Japanese box for medicines, worn at the sash
an ad, advertisement, promotes a product

explanation.surface: Pushing into territory by handing out pill boxes for publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: An inro is a small Japanese case for medicines, hung from the sash of a kimono.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance that intrudes on someone's territory or market is an intrusion into it.

clue.text: Poetic measure by poet left out? It's a pedestrian recourse

parts.note: a foot is a unit of metre in verse

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the poet's name

parts.note: Sylvia Plath, the American poet

explanation.surface: Verse rhythm from a poet who is excluded is a dull, ordinary resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' wants to mean dull, but it means someone on foot; PLATH loses L ('left out').
explanation.definitionFit: A way for people walking is a route someone on foot can turn to.

clue.text: Very sinful, like a spicy meal?

definitions.meaning: a devilled dish is cooked with hot, spicy seasoning

explanation.walkthrough: Devilled food is cooked with hot seasoning such as mustard or cayenne.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish wickedness belongs to the devil; devilled kidneys or eggs are hotly seasoned dishes.

clue.text: Breach of the peace in the Spencer fraternity?

parts.note: Diana Spencer, Princess Di, so 'the Spencer's' gives Di's
a religious order is a brotherhood

explanation.surface: Trouble in the Spencer family's brotherhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana, Princess of Wales, was born Diana Spencer, so 'the Spencer' is Di.
explanation.definitionFit: Public unrest or rioting is a disturbance of public calm, the legal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Elite unit protecting carrier miles ahead for tennis star

indicators.note: the regiment's letters wrap round and guard the rest

parts.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, an elite British army regiment

indicators.note: the letter for miles is moved to the front of the word for carrier

parts.note: a pram is a baby carriage

explanation.surface: Special forces guarding a vehicle that is miles in front, for a sports celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' moves the miles letter to the front of the carrier; 'protecting' wraps the regiment round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Pete Sampras was an American tennis player who won fourteen Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Person taking out second child half-heartedly

indicators.note: the word for child has two letters at its heart; losing one of them leaves it with half its heart

parts.note: a nipper is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone escorting another youngster on a date, without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking out' suggests a date; it means shooting. 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two middle Ps from NIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman who shoots targets from hiding is someone who eliminates them.

clue.text: Father with affectation carrying uncovered son — in this?

definitions.text: Father with affectation carrying uncovered son — in this?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the word for affectation holds the uncovered son inside it

parts.note: a pose is an affected manner

indicators.note: with its outside letters stripped off, the word son keeps only its middle

explanation.surface: A posing father carries his bare little boy in this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' son leaves O, which POSE is 'carrying'. The whole clue also describes the carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American baby carrier is worn on a parent's back to carry a child.

clue.text: Minor fashionable musical composition (not half)

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: the second half of the eight-letter word for the musical composition is dropped

parts.note: a fantasia is a free-form musical composition

explanation.surface: A trendy little piece of music, cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops the last four letters of FANTASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under the age of legal adulthood is a child in law.

clue.text: China might offer this benefit?

parts.note: china here is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate, mate), so a friend, not porcelain or the country

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means 'mate', so a china is a pal; the clue looks like it is about the country or crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The fellowship and friendly company a pal provides is what a mate offers.

clue.text: Growth in company significant after internal departures

indicators.note: once the inside letters of each word leave, only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: Expansion in a firm is meaningful after staff leave from inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' and 'company' suggest business; 'after internal departures' leaves only the ends of company and significant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is an abnormal sac that forms in the body, a kind of swelling or lump.

clue.text: Begin, say, current serial that's broadcast

indicators.note: the current follows the rearranged serial
broadcast as scattered seed, so the letters of serial are spread into a new order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Start, for instance, the present series being aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin' looks like a verb; it is Menachem Begin, prime minister of Israel. 'broadcast' rearranges SERIAL; I (current) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Menachem Begin was a prime minister of Israel, so an example of a citizen of that state.

clue.text: What was split in some dissection

indicators.note: the particle goes inside the word for some

parts.note: any, as in 'have you any?'
the atom was famously split by Rutherford's team

explanation.surface: Asks what was cut apart during an anatomical cutting-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatomy is also an old word for the act of cutting up a body; 'in' places the particle inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of bodily structure, learnt by cutting up bodies, once meant the act of cutting them up.

clue.text: Comfort in coffee as expected

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words coffee as expected

explanation.surface: Coffee gives the comfort you would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief from pain or worry, a state of relaxation, is being at rest.

clue.text: Casual worker fixing straight time for Broadway play

indicators.note: the casual worker is fixed round the word for straight, holding it in place

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
het, short for heterosexual
EST, Eastern Standard Time, the time zone of New York's Broadway

explanation.surface: A temporary employee arranging a direct time for a Broadway show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' puts TEMP round HET, giving THETEMP; EST is Eastern Standard Time, New York's zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance set on Prospero's island is a drama for the stage.
